#1398. Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

But this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an issue which Arteta must urgently address.

It is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

He obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

One back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7.

Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6).

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

After the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more quickly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

#1397. Roma draw 2-2 at PSG as Malen’s late penalty adds to Juventus’ December challenge

Roma came from behind to draw 2-2 with holders Paris Saint-Germain, with substitute Donyell Malen scoring a 78th-minute penalty. The leaders' rivals above Juventus showed the depth of their squad less than a month before they host Spalletti's side.

Roma left the Parc des Princes with a point and with their reputation enhanced. Mario Hermoso gave them the lead against the European champions. Paris Saint-Germain turned the game around through an Illia Zabarnyi header and an Ousmane Dembélé penalty.

In Europe, Malen’s spot-kick was his fifth goal. Across all competitions, it marked his 17th strike of the campaign, from 16 appearances. It came days after he scored four times in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. Yet he did not start in Paris, and neither did Paulo Dybala. Gian Piero Gasperini said he left Malen out because of the number of games he had played for Roma and the Netherlands.

That a reshuffled Roma could take a point in Paris says plenty about their squad. Luis Enrique’s side had not dropped points since a home defeat to Monaco on 4 September.

The result does not fix Roma’s European position. The club lists the game as Matchday 5 of the league phase. Roma have one win, two draws and two defeats so far. Under the format, clubs finishing 9th to 24th enter the play-offs, while 25th to 36th are knocked out. The top eight go straight into the round of 16.

That leaves Roma with work to do in a crowded December. Their next Champions League match is at home to Sporting CP on 8 December, kicking off at 21:00. They then travel to AEK Athens on 19 January and host Lille on 27 January 2027.

Domestically, Roma’s form has been strong. Their league record shows nine wins and three draws, with 36 goals scored and 11 conceded, Corriere dello Sport reported.

For Spalletti’s side, the schedule offers some contrast. After that European fixture, Roma play the derby away to Lazio on Sunday 13 December at 12:30. That leaves them six days between the derby and the visit of Juventus. Before travelling to Rome, Juventus are away to Como on 29 November. Udinese and Monza then come to Turin in Serie A, on 6 December and 14 December respectively.

Whether Roma’s European commitments take a toll remains to be seen. The evidence from Paris suggests Gasperini can rotate without a sharp drop in quality. Malen’s form, from the bench or from the start, will be a central concern for Juventus.

The two sides meet in round 16 of Serie A on Saturday 19 December 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1395. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

So who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”

Trevoh Chalobah will earn his third England cap in tonight’s Nations League match against Czech Republic. The Como centre-back, 27, played in the 6-4 defeat of France in the Bronze final at the World Cup and his other appearance for the Three Lions was in the defeat by Senegal last year.

Trent Alexander-Arnold will make his first England appearance in 15 months after being given a start. The Real Madrid full-back, who was not selected for the World Cup in the summer, earned his last cap against Andorra in 2025.

He replaces Jarell Quansah in Thomas Tuchel’s line-up that lost to Spain at the weekend.

“Trent had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us,” said Tuchel on the eve of the game at Fortuna Arena.

“We’re good. Everything is fine. He’s ready to go. He has qualities that you all know, like he’s strong on the ball, excellent crossing, good finishing. And very, very good on the ball. That’s basically what he brings.”

Ezri Konsa, who missed team training on the day before this game, is out. Morgan Rogers, meanwhile, steps in for Jude Bellingham in the No10 role as Tuchel looks to juggle four matches in 11 days during this extended international break.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line to make his first England start under head coach Thomas Tuchel for tonight’s Nations League game against Czech Republic.

Injuries to Nico O’Reilly and Ezri Konsa have forced Tuchel into changes at the back, with Alexander-Arnold expected to come in at right-back, Trevoh Chalobah to replace Konsa and Lewis Hall to step in for O’Reilly.

Alexander-Arnold has made only one appearance under Tuchel, as a substitute in a World Cup qualifying win against Andorra in June 2025. His last start for England came under interim head coach Lee Carsley, when he scored in a victory over Finland.

Jude Belllingham could be given a rest after playing the full 90 minutes in the defeat by Spain, which would give Morgan Rogers an opportunity in the No 10 position.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

#1394. Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s new biology skills wow scientists

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0)

Earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology company called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — including specialized protein-language models, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blog post, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu, Chen and others have found that the tool could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed new proteins, some of which behaved as expected when they were made and tested in the laboratory. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

The research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein-structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” says Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

But some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of the models’ abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

The unveiling of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster AI tool for protein-structure prediction, in 2020, launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with potential drugs, and for designing new proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but the LLMs have been used mostly as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich in Switzerland. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune conditions. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind to their target.

In other experiments, the OpenAI team showed that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and do other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blog post and technical paper.

Jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, thinks that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in each capability,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03836-z

#1393. Rasmus Hojlund MOCKS Man City as ex-Man United star is caught telling fans there is 'one team in Manchester' after scoring for Napoli - despite his former club lying in the Premier League relegation zone!

Published: 17:58 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EST, 24 November 2026

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

'Yeah, it's good banter,' he said on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

He would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

It was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'

#1392. Three above a 7, two below a 5: Fan player ratings for Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan

AC Milan rose from the canvas floor on the outskirt of Athens on Thursday night, coming from two goals down to beat Olympiacos 4-2.

With 50 minutes on the clock, Milan trailed by two goals after a Mike Maignan own-goal and a strike from Jota Silva. However, Omari Hutchinson inspired a comeback, halving the deficit with a great solo goal then setting up Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Diego Moreira scored on the break in the final seconds of added time to add a fourth and make sure of the victory, which boost the Rossoneri back into the top 24 with three games to go.

Looking at what our readers gave the players for the win in Piraeus, there is a real mixed bag of scores which in many ways matches the two-sided nature of the performance.

Starting with the negatives, Koni De Winter really struggled all night and played a stray pass for the second goal, which resulted in an average score of 4.5 out of 10 from our readers. Pervis Estupinan didn’t do much better, getting a 4.6.

Sankhoun Diawara had one of his tougher nights and got a 5, while Goncalo Ramos only got a 5.3 and Ardon Jashari also fell below a passing grade, but only just (5.9). Mike Maignan was scored a 6.1 and Adrien Rabiot a 6.2.

Then we get to the difference-makers: Diego Moreira averaged a 7, Alphadjo Cisse a 7.3 and Omari Hutchinson one of our highest grades of the season, with an outstanding 9 out of 10.

The subs were as follows: Yunus Musah got a 6.6, Christian Pulisic an 8.1, Fikayo Tomori a 7/1, Filippo Terracciano a 5.9 and Christian Comotto a 6.1.

#1391. Francisco Conceição has a hand in three goals as Juventus beat Omonia Nicosia 4-1

Juventus came from behind to beat Omonia Nicosia at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday night, scoring four times in the fifth round of the UEFA Europa League league stage after falling behind in the 15th minute.

The visitors went ahead through Šatka, with Tanković providing the assist. Omonia had already had Tănase booked in the 10th minute, and Juventus saw Lucumí cautioned in the 34th.

Luciano Spalletti’s side, set up in a 3-4-2-1, levelled three minutes after that booking when Cambiaso scored from Francisco Conceição’s assist. Six minutes later Ekhator put Juventus in front, again with Conceição supplying the final pass, and the home side went in at half-time a goal to the good.

Conceição got on the scoresheet himself in the 68th minute, and Boga made it four five minutes later, with Cambiaso the provider this time. Balkovec was booked for Omonia in the 81st minute.

Cambiaso was rated 8.93, the highest on the pitch, after a goal, an assist, 4 shots and 3 key passes. Conceição, rated 8.61, was involved in three of the goals and had 7 shots and 4 key passes before being replaced with 86 minutes played. Boga and Ekhator also scored, the latter in 66 minutes on the pitch, while Neto made 4 saves.

Juventus had 60% of the ball and completed 570 of their 619 passes, against 351 of 410 for Omonia. They had 23 shots to 13, with 9 on target to 5, and finished with expected goals of 2.42 to 1.13. Kaminski made 5 saves in the Omonia goal.

— OMONOIA FC (@OMONOIAfootball) November 26, 2026

The win is Juventus’s second in a row with four goals, following the 4-0 victory over Venezia, and leaves them unbeaten in five matches in all competitions since their defeat to Genoa. In that run they have also beaten Napoli and AZ Alkmaar and drawn with Fiorentina.

For Omonia, it is a second defeat in their last four matches, after a draw with Apoel Nicosia, a win over Anorthosis and a loss to NEC Nijmegen.

Juventus return to Serie A on Sunday 29 November away to Como. Omonia go back to the Cypriot First Division on Monday 30 November, when they visit Nea Salamis.

#1390. Moretto: Krösche ‘will bring a name’ to Milan with him but not Hardung – the situation

Markus Krösche will soon begin his work as AC Milan’s new Head of Football, but Timmo Hardung will not be joining him.

It has not been a well-kept secret that Milan have wanted to welcome Krösche as the new head of the management since the summer. Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall a few months ago, but the German has since left his position and now seems all set for a new adventure in Italy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Compensation has been agreed to release him fully from Eintracht, and the only question mark swirling concerned whether he would be joined by his right-hand man Hardung, with whom he has worked for years.

In a video published on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto took stock of the situation regarding the possible arrival of Hardung at Milan as sporting director alongside Krösche. His words are via MilanNews.

“I wanted to focus on Timmo Hardung, in the sense that I would like to specify a situation linked to the Rossoneri organisation that already exists, what he will become and what could be in the future,” he said.

“Everything has been said about Krosche at AC Milan and we are only waiting for the official announcement. Krosche will certainly bring someone with him, but this person, at the moment, is not Timmo Hardung, sporting director of Eintracht, Krosche’s right-hand man for a long time.

“There’s been talk that Hardung isn’t coming to Milan because of a deteriorating relationship with Markus Krösche. I actually wanted to deny this, in the sense that the two are on very good terms and still have a great rapport. This summer, the two worked closely together at Eintracht. So, in fact, they have an excellent relationship.

“If Hardung doesn’t join Krosche at Milan as sporting director, it’s certainly for other reasons, namely that perhaps there’s no room for Hardung in the structure and organisation designed by Gerry Cardinale. So it would be a choice tied to other dynamics within the Rossoneri.

“I can confirm that Krosche will bring one name, we’ll see if he then adds another name, which would be Hardung, but I think we’ll find out later. Contacts are in progress, but it’s not yet 100% clear whether Hardung will be able to join Krosche.”

#1389. Mariani to referee Como v Juventus, with Como still without a win under him

Maurizio Mariani of the Aprilia section will take charge of Como v Juventus at the Sinigaglia, a direct fight for the Champions League places. Como have never won with him in charge, and his recent record has brought friction with Inter and with Francisco Conceição.

Maurizio Mariani of the Aprilia section will referee Como v Juventus at the Sinigaglia on Sunday 29 November at 20:45. The AIA named Peretti and Perrotti as his assistants. Marinelli will be fourth official. Pezzuto is on VAR, with Meraviglia as AVAR.

Como have never won with Mariani in charge. For Juventus, the appointment comes in a direct fight for the Champions League places. Spalletti’s side are sixth and Como fifth, so a win at the Sinigaglia would close the gap on a direct rival.

Mariani’s name came up last season in Milan prosecutors’ wiretaps in the so-called ‘Arbitropoli’ case, Tuttosport reported. Those conversations discussed referees said to be welcome or unwelcome to Inter. Inter president Beppe Marotta also strongly criticised a penalty Mariani gave Napoli against Inter on 25 October 2025. He called it a ‘rigorino’, meaning a soft penalty.

The Juventus link is more direct. Francisco Conceição has had a goal disallowed by Mariani. The paper calls the referee a nightmare for the Portuguese winger. That disallowed goal was not the only troubled meeting between the two.

Both video officials will also work the night before. Pezzuto is assistant VAR for Torino v Lazio on Saturday 28 November at 18:00. Meraviglia runs the VAR for Inter v Genoa later that evening.

After 12 rounds, Como have won eight, drawn two and lost two. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10. Juventus have won six, drawn three and lost three, with a 19-12 goal record. Spalletti has called the Como game a key moment after the win over Omonia.

Como will come into Sunday’s game with two more days of rest than Juventus. Spalletti countered that players returning from injury let him plan for the Como game as well. Before the Omonia game, Nico González and Kalulu had not recovered, along with the long-term absentees.

#1388. Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan: Five things we learned – a breakout night and a glaring issue

AC Milan went into their Europa League fixture against Olympiacos in need of a win to get the ball rolling, and win they did.

The eventual 2-4 scoreline only tells part of the story, as Ruben Amorim’s side had to battle back from two goals down. Lorenzo Pirola’s header drew what was officially an own-goal from Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva doubled the lead after a slack pass from Koni De Winter was punished.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the Omari Hutchinson show. The Englishman gave Milan hope with a wonderful solo goal, before turning provider for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround. Diego Moreira’s late goal on the counter made sure of a very important three points.

So, the Diavolo return to Italy with smiles on their faces, cultivating the hopes of a play-off spot and keeping the top eight dream alive too. Ivan Stoev has picked out five major talking points from a dramatic night on the outskirts of Athens.

Omari Hutchinson has had mixed performances when given the opportunities since his arrival in the summer and the feeling is that he had plenty of work to do in order to justify the hefty optional price tag on his loan contract. Games like the one against Olympiacos are just the type of opportunities for the attacker to prove his abilities.

The Nottingham Forest loanee didn’t get off to the best start as Milan struggled in the opening 45 minutes with their opponents pressing very high and aggressively. This starved him of possession in a central role and he didn’t get the ball to his feet much, let alone with space to run at.

In the second half, however, Hutchinson moved to a wider role on the right flank and he immediately started causing trouble for the Greeks.

In the 56th minute it was an impressive solo run by the Englishman that started Milan’s comeback as the winger picked up the ball in his own half and carried it all the way to the opponent’s penalty box, before cutting onto his left foot and beating the keeper with a tidy finish in the far post.

Milan fez uma grande reviravolta na segunda parte em casa do Olympiacos, com Omari Hutchinson em destaque. https://t.co/RsOgYVqrP7

Seven minutes later Hutchinson continued to cause trouble down that flank. This time around he found Cisse with a lovely cross and the youngster made no mistake to bury it and bring the scores level.

The former Arsenal academy man wasn’t finished yet though: in the 71st minute he provided yet another inviting cross into the penalty box which found Pulisic, who applied a lovely volleyed finish to make it 3-2.

Hutchinson then continued to be a menace in transition as he showed relentlessness even in the dying minutes. A corner was cleared and he picked up possession, somehow beat a man and ran with it, getting the ‘hockey assist’ for Moreira’s goal.

It was an absolutely brilliant second-half performance and if he finds continuity then that option to buy might just before more appealing, or at the very least a re-negotiation to keep him permanently. The issue is that the Olympiacos owner also owns Forest, and he saw that display first-hand.

The goals Milan conceded were quite preventable yet again. The feeling is definitely growing as January approaches that the back line needs a true leader in the middle of a defence that continues to be error-prone.

Mario Gila has looked like a bargain of a signing and he has been superb, but he is playing mostly as a right-back/outside centre-back. Strahinja Pavlovic remains a key player as well, but the same applies as with Gila just on the left side.

Koni De Winter is just not a man that you can trust to anchor the rearguard to a high level most weeks. He’s had some stellar performances – the game against Inter comes to mind – but he often follows up those performance with some shocking ones.

Matteo Gabbia is definitely better in terms of leadership and keeping things tidy, but we will need to wait and see if he features in Amorim’s long-term plans. He’s been injured for quite a while too, so a reacclimatisation period will be required.

Sankhoun Diawara also looked very shaky in Greece, but this in itself proves a point because the idea cannot have been for him to start as many games as he has. It just further signals that someone who can play down the middle and steady everything could be the difference this season and beyond.

Ardon Jashari got his first Milan goal at the weekend in the win over Frosinone. Then, the unfortunate injury to Luka Modric leading up to the Olympiacos game meant he was given the chance to prove himself, after a few shaky performances this season.

Excluding a few misplaces passes in the first half, the Swiss international was solid enough. There wasn’t anything flashy but also no errors leading to goal, which was a relief.  The stats say that he had 77 touches, completed 58/64 passes (91%), had 1 big chance created, 2 tackles, 7 recoveries and 1 clearance. He also won 2/2 aerial duels and 2 ground duels, committing just 1 foul.

Speaking of chances being seized, it’s worth giving a shoutout to Fikayo Tomori who came on for a struggling De Winter. Milan looked much more solid with the Englishman on the pitch as he showcased his athleticism but also his experienced reading of the game.

The professionalism shown by Tomori must be respected given the centre-back was excluded from the squad in the summer and put on the transfer market. He worked hard to prove that he deserves to stay and to play. Now, the next mission is to earn what currently seems like an unlikely renewal.

In the first half Milan were struggling with the high press and the limited space, so they had limited chances going forward. The second half was a completely different story especially with Yunus Musah and Pulisic coming on for Estupinan and Goncalo Ramos.

We have already mentioned Hutchinson ran the show, but Pulisic was also crucial as he scored an impressive volley which is hard to execute by any standard,  and he then goal the assist that made the final 4-2. He should’ve really scored another one, but we’ll give him a well-earned pass.

Moreira was also heavily in the mix and at times he was frustrating with his end product being lacking, though the direct nature of his pace and dribbling were a joy to watch again. Having a player who picks up the ball and says ‘Fine, I’ll do it’ is really refreshing. His defensive effort as a wing-back was not lacking either.

Cisse all in all had a quiet game yet found his name up in lights on the scoreboard for a 10th time this season with a tidy headed finish. The knack that he has for being in the right place at the right time is something that is so impressive in a 20-year-old. A pay rise could be on the way to fend off calls from England.

We have to give the coach his flowers too, don’t we. The first half wasn’t good but it was still better compared to some other European performances this season. The goal was very preventable, but the Rossoneri did well not to fold under the pressure Olympiacos were applying.

In the second half the coach made two changes which improved the team quite a bit, though one of them was forced as Ramos was injured. Amorim revealed after the game that he knew the Greek side couldn’t keep up their high press for 90 minutes, which would yield spaces to attack in the second half.

Shifting Hutchinson to the right was also the correct choice, as was taking off De Winter for Tomori, and also letting Cisse play as a centre-forward. Depending on how Ramos is, he might have to do the same in Cagliari.

Finally, it is worth mentioning the attitude was completely different as opposed to the game against Ferencvaros. The desire and belief that the game could be turned around offers some encouragement that this team cannot just get into the knockout stages, but can give anyone a game if they show up.

#1387. Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

“My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, says Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, said Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts currently on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration

Ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang said.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty

#1386. The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United plan to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget…

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

In the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – important given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ said Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’

Pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

#1385. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.
